H1_T_COMPLETE_TO_TPRIME.claim: For every s in T and t in T', st is an edge; hence T is complete to T'.
proof: Fix arbitrary s in T and t in T'.
Consider the ordered seven vertices z-y-s-p-m-n-t.
Consecutive edges zy, ys, sp, pm, mn, nt hold from the C11/source/type/111 facts.
z is nonadjacent to s,p,m,n,t because z lies in descendant Y0' and is anticomplete to the enlarged seed, which contains old S and stored support.
y is nonadjacent to p,n by the frozen stable set, to m by the source orientation, and to t because y has old type T while t lies in disjoint T'.
s is nonadjacent to m because m lies in old Y0 and old axiom (iii) makes Y0 anticomplete to old seed S; s is nonadjacent to n because n has type T' and s is not in T'.
p is nonadjacent to n by stored 111/stability and to t because p has type T.
m is nonadjacent to t because m lies in old Y0 and t lies in old seed.
Thus the only possible chord is st.
If st were absent, z-y-s-p-m-n-t would be an induced P7, contradicting P7-freeness.
Therefore st is forced for arbitrary s,t.

H2_TYPES_ARE_STABLE.claim: T and T' are stable sets.
proof: All vertices of T receive the same seed color alpha because f(T) is a singleton.
All vertices of T' receive the same seed color beta because f(T') is a singleton.
The seed coloring f is proper.
Hence no two vertices of T are adjacent, and no two vertices of T' are adjacent.
H2_TYPES_ARE_STABLE.consequence: G[T union T'] is the complete bipartite graph K_{|T|,|T'|}.

H3_CANONICAL_H8.claim: For every s in T and t in T', the eight vertices {s,t,p,m,n,y,y',z} induce one canonical labeled graph H8.
proof_notes: s-p,s-y and t-n,t-y' are exact type adjacencies.
m-y' is the forced closing edge from PASS_C11_P7_SURVIVOR_RIGIDITY.
z-y,z-y' are the residual COMMON attachments.
m-z is absent because z in descendant Y0' is anticomplete to the enlarged seed and m is in that seed.
All other nonedges follow from exact types, old Y0 anticompleteness to old seed, the frozen stable set {y,y',p,n}, z anticomplete to stored support, and the source orientation ym nonedge.

H4_FORCED_CYCLES.proof: All cycle edges and all absent chords are read directly from the exact H8 edge/nonedge table.

proof: Because y has old type T with singleton seed color alpha, L(y)=[4]\{alpha}.
Because y' has old type T' with singleton seed color beta, L(y')=[4]\{beta}.
The previously proved survivor rigidity gives L(y)\L(y')={f'(m)}.
But [4]\{alpha} minus [4]\{beta} is exactly {beta}.
Therefore f'(m)=beta.
Legacy 111 Q-admissibility requires f'(p),f'(n) to avoid f(T) union f(T')={alpha,beta}.
Since L(y)=[4]\{alpha} and L(y')=[4]\{beta}, their intersection is [4]\{alpha,beta}.

canonical_H8.pendant_description_from_prior_kernel: Within the prior seven-vertex survivor subset {y',z,y,s,p,m,n}, n is pendant at m; adding arbitrary t in T' forces the complete T-T' bridge and closes the full H8.

general_form.c(y),c(y_prime): members of [4]\{alpha,beta} in any acceptability-violation extension

color_kernel.interpretation: m is a duplicate opposite-type color anchor: its color beta is already excluded from y' by the old seed-neighbors of type T', so the forced edge m-y' preserves y' list while closing the forbidden P7.

scientific_interpretation.strongest_supported_statement: Every frozen-authority C11 P7 survivor contains, for every choice s in T and t in T', the same canonical induced H8. The old type sets form a complete bipartite bridge, H8 contains one forced C6 and two forced C5s, f'(m) equals the opposite type color beta, and the stored endpoints p,n are colored from the common two-color intersection of the two 3-lists.
not_claimed: that H8 alone yields a repair
that quotienting H8 is sound or polynomially complete
that C1S, CS1 or CSS are reachable or unreachable
